name: יְהוֹשָׁפָט
summary: Chiefly the king of Judah, son of Asa, who walked in the first ways of David, sent princes, Levites and priests through Judah with the book of the law, set judges in its fortified cities and charged them that they judged “not for man but for Yahweh”, and, when Moab, Ammon and Mount Seir came against him, prayed “our God, will you not judge them?” and was delivered (2Ch 17–20); he is in Jesus’ genealogy (Mat 1:8). Also David’s recorder, son of Ahilud; Solomon’s officer in Issachar, son of Paruah; the father of Jehu, king of Israel; and, spelt יוֹשָׁפָט, one of David’s mighty men and a priest who blew the trumpet before the ark. The name is the divine name in its short form יְהוֹ and שָׁפָט, “he has judged”: “Yahweh has judged”, that is, has done justice and delivered. Joel names the place where Yahweh will judge the nations the valley of Jehoshaphat, and explains it: “there I will sit to judge” (Jol 4:12).

evidence.note: “Let the nations come up to the valley of יְהוֹשָׁפָט, for there I will sit to judge (לִשְׁפֹּט) all the nations round about”: the name read as Yahweh judging.
“I will bring them down to the valley of יְהוֹשָׁפָט, and I will enter into judgment (וְנִשְׁפַּטְתִּי) with them there.”
“יְהוֹשָׁפָט son of Asa began to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab.”
“Yahweh was with יְהוֹשָׁפָט, because he walked in the first ways of David his father.”
His officers taught in Judah, with the book of the law of Yahweh.
“He set judges (שֹׁפְטִים) in the land … and said to the judges, Consider what you do, for you judge (תִּשְׁפְּטוּ) not for man but for Yahweh.”
“Our God, will you not judge (תִשְׁפָּט) them? For we have no strength against this great multitude.”
After the deliverance they blessed Yahweh in the valley of Berachah.
“The son of יְהוֹשָׁפָט, who sought Yahweh with all his heart.”
He asks for a prophet of Yahweh and is sent to Elisha son of שָׁפָט.
Ἰωσαφάτ in the genealogy of Jesus Christ.
“Jehu son of יְהוֹשָׁפָט son of Nimshi.” So 9:14.
“וְיוֹשָׁפָט the Mithnite”, among David’s mighty men.
וְיוֹשָׁפָט among the priests blowing the trumpets before the ark.

note: BDB files the name under הוה (e.az.bb, n.pr.m and n.pr.loc), with the variant יוֹשָׁפָט; it is linked here to the shaphat entry for its verb, as elishama is linked to shama. The key also holds the valley of Jehoshaphat (Jol 4:2, 12), a place, which has no person record. TIPNR keys the two men spelt יוֹשָׁפָט as Joshaphat. The Phoenician name-type špṭbʿl, “Baal has judged”, is the same formation with another god’s name (see the phn-shptbl cognate).
